item.content:encoded:
Apple India Rolls In Profits

Apple’s India story is no longer just about iPhone sales. In FY26, the smartphone maker’s local unit saw record growth in revenue and profit, while exports and launch of new services further deepened its foothold. So, as component shortages loom, can Apple sustain its India surge?

An Expanding Ecosystem: Apple India’s FY26 performance reflected strong demand across iPhones, Macs, iPads and other products. Revenue from traded goods drove most of the growth, while services such as AppleCare and maintenance contracts further added to the revenue mix.

Here is a quick look at Apple India’s FY26 numbers:

  • Net profit rose 66% YoY to ₹5,311 Cr
  • Operating revenue grew 31.4% YoY to ₹1.04 Lakh Cr
  • Total Expenses also rose 28% YoY to ₹96,224 Cr

The numbers show Apple is building a broader consumer technology business in India rather than relying solely on its flagship smartphone.

The Cost Conundrum: However, Apple’s growth came with a steep price tag. Inventory purchases remained its largest financial drain in FY26, while licensing fees more than doubled to ₹10,374 Cr. Employee costs and marketing expenditure also rose substantially as Apple expanded its operations and strengthened its presence in India.

The India Playbook: All said and done, Apple’s ambitions in India extend beyond sales. The country has become one of its largest production bases outside China, with iPhone exports crossing ₹2 Lakh Cr in FY26. At the same time, it is also expanding its services ecosystem in India. 

The OEM has launched new offerings such as Apple Pay and Fitness+ in the past few months, which are expected to create new revenue streams for the iPhone maker going forward.

The Sombre Outlook: But Apple’s near-term momentum faces pressure due to chip and memory shortages. As such, the company expects supply chain constraints to impact iPhones, Macs and iPads globally, potentially influencing product availability in India.

With demand rising, manufacturing deepening and services entering the ecosystem, here is how Apple fared on the financial front in FY26…

From The Editor’s Desk

Flipkart’s Food Delivery Foray

  • The Walmart-owned ecommerce major plans to roll out its food delivery service, called Eat-in by Minutes, to the general public by October-end this year. The company is said to have expanded its internal pilot in Bengaluru to more than 8,000 employees.
  • Flipkart, which began piloting food delivery internally earlier this year, plans to expand the service to six cities by 2026-end. It has tapped the state-backed ONDC for restaurant onboarding and has also deployed a dedicated fleet of riders via its logistics arm Ekart. 
  • Flipkart’s planned launch comes as new rivals take on Zomato and Swiggy. Rapido is offering a zero-commission model to attract eateries to its new foodtech platform Ownly. Swish has also begun piloting food delivery survive in select Bengaluru pincodes.

New Twist In Satcom Saga

  • The Centre is considering developing a hardware device to oversee services offered by Starlink and other overseas satcom operators. All traffic will be routed via the proposed device, which will act as a control layer between users and satellite networks.
  • The government is considering involving public sector R&D units, while keeping participation by select private players open. With this, officials are looking to address risks associated with foreign satellite operators.
  • The plan comes right after Elon Musk accused certain Indian “oligarchs” of blocking Starlink’s entry into India. The Centre has denied allegations of preferential treatment, maintaining that all applicants are at the same regulatory stage.

IndiaMART Under CCPA Radar

  • The Central Consumer Protection Authority has pulled up seven ecommerce platforms, including IndiaMART and Justdial, for listing and selling unauthorised hazardous explosives such as ammonium nitrate, gun powder, picric acid and PETN.
  • The regulatory action resulted in the delisting of 3,940 sellers and listing entries, including 3.092 at IndiaMART and 206 at Justdial. The CCPA also imposed penalties worth ₹30 Lakh on two platforms namely Dial4Trade and ExportersIndia. 
  • The development comes amid regulatory clampdown on new-age tech consumer brands. Just days ago, CCPA imposed a fine of ₹10 Lakh on Rapido over unfair trade practices. FSSAI has also issued notices to multiple D2C brands and quick commerce players.

Founder FY26 Salary Tracker

  • Twenty-two founders across 15 Indian new-age tech companies earned a combined ₹66.87 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26, up 2.3% from ₹65.34 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. Of these, 16 received increases in fixed pay and four saw reductions. 
  • Honasa cofounder Ghazal Alagh saw her fixed remuneration soar 60% YoY to ₹2.4 Cr in FY26, while Delhivery cofounder Sahil Barua followed with a 21.4% YoY jump to ₹3.4 Cr. Ola Electric founder Bhavish Aggarwal’s salary fell 34.8% to ₹4.5 Cr.
  • MobiKwik’s Bipin Preet Singh and Upasana Taku were the most paid founders, drawing fixed remuneration of ₹6.3 Cr each in FY26. Lenskart cofounder Peyush Bansal followed at ₹5.7 Cr, down 1.7% from ₹5.8 Cr.

Decoding Burma Burma DRHP

  • Last week, the restaurant chain’s parent entity, Hunger Pangs Limited, filed its DRHP with SEBI. The proposed IPO consists of a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹150 Cr and an OFS component of up to 2.79 Cr shares.
  • As per the draft IPO papers, Hunger Pangs has 110 shareholders. Cofounders Ankit Gupta and Chirag Chhajer each hold a 33.35% stake. Its cap table remains heavily concentrated, with top eight stakeholders collectively owning 83.19% in the company.
  • Negen Capital, via its  two funds, holds about 10% stake in the company, while rubber and plastic manufacturing company Bbigplas Poly also owns a 2.72% stake. Venture Catalysts also holds around 1.88% stake in Burma Burma. 

Inc42 Markets

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

How Protein Pantry Is Reimagining Vegetarian Protein

On-the-go snacking and quick meals are becoming the norm for the Indian urban milieu. On this front, choices remain very limited for vegetarians. To solve this, Protein Pantry is building a portfolio of clean-label, high-protein snacks and meals that are designed for quick preparation.

Protein For Daily Needs: Founded in 2025, Protein Pantry sells a range of ready-to-cook frozen foods such as soya chaap, kebabs, cutlets and falafels. The brand claims that its products are baked rather than fried, with no maida, preservatives or palm oil. Each item can be prepared in under three minutes, targeting users who want a protein-rich meal without lengthy cooking.

Healthy Early Traction: Protein Pantry claims to have so far served around 30,000 users and is currently clocking a revenue run rate of ₹7 Cr. It also operates a 10,000+ sq ft facility in Noida and sells its offerings through its website and quick-commerce platforms.

The Road Ahead: Backed by Sharrp Ventures and Indian Silicon Valley Capital, the startup plans to now focus on scaling manufacturing and expanding distribution. Currently operating in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, Protein Pantry plans to expand to more cities in the long-term.

With the Indian frozen food market projected to become a ₹64,364 Cr opportunity by 2034, can Protein Pantry make high-protein food a daily habit for Indians?

Infographic Of The Day

India’s condiment game is getting a glow-up. From pudina chutney and chilli oil to peri-peri mayo and dips, homegrown D2C brands are leaving no stone unturned to grab a pie of the thriving Indian condiment market. So, which startups are adding the extra tadka to our plates…

item.title: Can Hotels Become ixigo’s Fourth Growth Engine?
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Travel tech company ixigo is betting on hotels as its fourth growth engine alongside trains, flights, and buses, as further…
item.content:encoded:
Travel tech company ixigo is betting on hotels as its fourth growth engine alongside trains, flights, and buses, as further market share gains become harder in rail bookings and high airfares and capacity constraints weigh on flights.

The company began reporting hotels as a separate operating segment in Q2 FY27, breaking it out from ‘Others’. The revenue of the hotel segment grew more than sixfold to ₹8.1 Cr, accounting for 2.5% of ixigo’s ₹321 Cr operating revenue in the September quarter.

Its gross transaction value (GTV) reached ₹111.3 Cr, or 2.6X the year-ago figure, making it ixigo’s fastest-growing business line by this measure.

“Hotels took a great leap forward, getting to a critical mark that makes it large enough to start disclosing (separately),” ixigo group CEO Alok Bajpai said during the earnings call.

The segment’s contribution loss widened to ₹1.2 Cr from ₹71 Lakh in Q2 FY26. However, the contribution margin improved to -15% from -55%, as revenue growth outpaced the increase in direct costs.

This loss captures only part of the investment. Much of ixigo’s hotel-related technology, product, and employee spending sits within group costs. Management attributed around ₹10 Cr of the approximately ₹20 Cr increase in group costs, excluding ESOP expenses, to building and scaling hotels.

Its train, flight, and bus businesses generated around ₹126 Cr in contribution profit during the quarter, helping fund the expansion. 

As Inc42’s earlier business model analysis examined, ixigo is reinvesting operating leverage from its established businesses into hotels, AI, and brand building. The latest results show how it is pursuing hotel growth through existing customers and direct property partnerships.

ixigo’s Hotel Blueprint

ixigo is targeting budget and mid-market accommodation, particularly independent hotels, to serve travellers who already book journeys through its platforms but may use offline channels or other services for accommodation.

“The opportunity is particularly compelling in the budget, mid-market, and independent hotels, where online penetration is low, and travellers need greater reliability and peace of mind,” Bajpai said during the earnings call.


Industry estimates cited by the company’s management put India’s hotel market at ₹1.57 Lakh Cr in FY26, projected to reach ₹1.94 Lakh Cr by FY28. Hotel bookings through OTAs are expected to rise from ₹40,200 Cr to ₹57,000 Cr over the same period.

About 60% of hotel room nights in India sell for less than ₹2,000 a night, while independent hotels account for 73% of rooms.

This market overlaps with ixigo’s customer base – 94% of its transactions involve travellers going to or from Tier II and III cities, while more than nine in 10 trips booked are by train or bus.

More than 86% of Q2 hotel bookings came from existing users, which management believes can help it scale without acquiring every hotel customer separately.

ixigo has more than 70,000 hotels on its platforms, including over 12,000 directly contracted properties across around 1,100 towns. Direct partnerships stood at over 10,000 properties across nearly 700 towns in the previous quarter. The company said HELLO, its AI-first hotel partner platform, helped accelerate this expansion.

The Q2 figures also include Brevistay, in which ixigo acquired a 54.66% stake for ₹65.69 Cr. The startup offers rooms for three, six, or 12 hours rather than a full-day stay. ixigo is using the acquisition to expand direct hotel relationships, meaning reported growth includes both organic expansion and Brevistay’s contribution.

While ixigo builds its hotel business, its three established verticals continue to fund the expansion, with differing growth prospects across trains, flights, and buses.

How Are ixigo’s Core Businesses Performing? 

The number of train passenger journeys booked through ixigo rose around 7% YoY to 2.9 Cr in Q2 FY27. Revenue increased 16% to ₹149.1 Cr and contribution profit grew 29% to ₹47.2 Cr.

Management said ixigo’s share of the OTA rail market reached around 64%. With railway capacity growing at an estimated 4-5% annually, further expansion will increasingly depend on new products, monetisation, and cross-selling, alongside booking volumes.


Trains’ share of GTV has fallen from more than half to the low-40% range as other categories expand. Management expects this proportion to decline further, even as the business grows in absolute terms.

Flight GTV increased 37% YoY, but revenue declined 8% to ₹82.7 Cr. The gross take rate fell to 7% from 9.4%, reflecting pressure on monetisation amid higher airfares, capacity constraints, and a changing booking mix. Higher ticket values supported GTV but did not translate into revenue growth.

The festive season provided some support to flight bookings, but management cautioned that the recovery remains uncertain as high airfares and capacity constraints continue to weigh on demand. 

“We hope this improves as the peak of the festive season arrives, though it is too early to call, and this should not be read as guidance,” ixigo said in its earnings release. 

Buses remained a stronger growth channel. Bus GTV increased 32% YoY to ₹752.65 Cr, revenue grew 24% to ₹81.04 Cr, and contribution profit rose 27% to ₹43.14 Cr.

These established businesses provide the earnings and customer reach to support hotels. The challenge is to convert that advantage into sustained growth while managing expansion costs that extend beyond the segment’s reported contribution loss.

item.title: Burma Burma DRHP: A Look At Shareholding Pattern & Key Executives
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Last week, Hunger Pangs Limited, the parent company of restaurant chain Burma Burma, filed its DRHP with SEBI, proposing a…
item.content:encoded:
Last week, Hunger Pangs Limited, the parent company of restaurant chain Burma Burma, filed its DRHP with SEBI, proposing a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹150 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.79 Cr shares.

Hunger Pangs has 110 shareholders, including its promoters and public shareholders. Cofounders Ankit Gupta and Chirag Chhajer each hold a 33.35% stake in the company and plan to offload up to 60 Lakh shares each.

Negen Capital, through its Negen Undiscovered Value Fund and Negen Tech Opportunities Angel Fund, holds about 10% stake in the company. The investment firm first invested in Hunger Pangs in November 2022 and doubled down in 2023.

Hunger Pangs’ shareholding remains concentrated, with its top eight shareholders collectively holding 83.19% of the company on a fully diluted basis.

Among the other shareholders, rubber and plastic manufacturing company Bbigplas Poly Private Limited holds a 2.72% stake, while Venture Catalysts owns 1.88%. Individual investors, including Sagun Capital founder Saket Agarwal and Nazara backer Nisarg Ajaykumar Vakharia, each hold about 1% stake in Hunger Pangs.

Burma Burma’s Business

Meanwhile, the fresh issue will help Burma Burma expand its restaurant network, with plans to open 27 company-owned outlets in new Tier I and Tier II cities. The company expects to open 12 outlets in FY28 and another 15 in FY29. The funds will cover civil and interior work, kitchen equipment and other setup costs.

To note, Burma Burma opened its first restaurant in Mumbai in 2014 and specialises in vegetarian Burmese cuisine. As of July 31, 2026, the chain operated 22 restaurants across nine cities, including Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Delhi NCR. It also operated a delivery kitchen in Mumbai and three warehouses.

The chain operates in the broader Asian dining segment, competing with restaurant brands such as Mainland China, Mamagoto, Yum Yum Cha and Berco’s.

In March 2026, Burma Burma raised ₹38 Cr at a valuation of ₹500 Cr. The round was led by Negen Capital, with participation from Endurance Capital and Coheron Wealth. The company’s total private funding to date stands at about $11 Mn.

Hunger Pangs’ net loss surged to ₹15.4 Cr in FY26 from ₹50 Lakh in FY25, while operating revenue rose 46.6% YoY to ₹155.5 Cr from ₹106.1 Cr. Dine-in contributed 88.82% of operating revenue in FY26, while delivery accounted for 10.76%.

Who’s At Burma Burma’s Helm?

Board of Directors

Shivakumar Dega

Dega has served as chairman and independent director at Hunger Pangs since July 2026. He has been an operating partner at Advent International since April 2023, according to his LinkedIn profile. He also serves on the boards of companies including iD Fresh, Intellect Design Arena, Leapfrog Strategy Consulting, PGP Glass and Yes Bank.

Ankit Virendra Gupta

Gupta is the cofounder and joint managing director of Hunger Pangs. After completing his management trainee programme at The Taj Mahal Palace in Mumbai, he worked in hotel operations for about two years. Around 2011, he returned to his family business before launching Burma Burma with Chhajer.

Chirag Narendra Chhajer

Chhajer is the cofounder and joint managing director of Hunger Pangs. He graduated in international business from Swinburne University in Melbourne, Australia, in 2008. He subsequently joined Chhajer Synthetics, his family’s textile trading business, before cofounding Burma Burma with Gupta.

Kushal Budhia

Budhia joined Hunger Pangs as an independent director in July 2026. He is the cofounder and group CFO of BetterPlace. Before joining BetterPlace, he spent more than two years at Pepperfry. Over a career spanning 17 years, he has also worked with Barbeque Nation Hospitality, Jupiter Capital and Goldman Sachs.

Lavanya Nalli Ramanathan

Ramanathan joined Hunger Pangs as an independent director in September 2026. She has served as vice chairman of Nalli Silk Sarees since January 2016. Her previous experience includes roles at Myntra and McKinsey. She also serves on the boards of Nalli Silk Sarees and Etnische Fashions.

Pavitra Joshi Singh

Singh joined Hunger Pangs as an independent director in September 2026. She is the chief human resources officer and vice president for PepsiCo India and South Asia, where she has held various leadership roles over a 20-year career.

Key Managerial Personnel And Senior Management

Vishnu Kumar Agarwal

Agarwal joined Burma Burma in 2014 and was elevated to CFO in 2026. His total compensation for FY26 stood at ₹58.5 Lakh.

Abhinav Agarwal

Agarwal was designated company secretary in May 2026 and compliance officer in September 2026. He joined Hunger Pangs in April 2026. Before this, he served as AVP of finance, strategy, legal and investor relations at BRISKPE. He has more than a decade of experience and has also worked with Vayana, theremin.ai and Pantomath Capital Advisors.

Ansab Ajaz Khan

Khan joined Burma Burma in 2014 and was appointed chief of kitchen operations in September 2026. He has previously worked with Mahindra Holidays and Resorts India and Mehul Restaurant and Bar. His total compensation for FY26 was ₹78 Lakh.

Sahil Mohan

Mohan was appointed chief of restaurant operations in September 2026, after 12 years with Burma Burma. He previously worked with Indian Hotels Company Limited and Taj Lands End, Mumbai. His total compensation for FY26 was ₹59.4 Lakh.

Pooja Soman

Soman joined Hunger Pangs in November 2024 and was elevated to chief human resources officer in April 2026. She has more than 17 years of experience in human resources management. Her total compensation for FY26 stood at ₹43.4 Lakh.

item.title: IndiaMART, Justdial Booked By CCPA Over Explosive Products Listings
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has taken regulatory action against seven ecommerce platforms, including IndiaMART and Justdial, over the…
item.content:encoded:
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has taken regulatory action against seven ecommerce platforms, including IndiaMART and Justdial, over the listing and sales of unauthorised hazardous explosives.

The material listed on these platforms included ammonium nitrate, gun powder, picric acid and pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN).

Except for ammonium nitrate, all of the aforementioned chemicals are exclusively used in manufacturing explosives.

The regulatory action has resulted in the delisting of 3,940 sellers and listing entries, while the authority has imposed penalties totalling ₹30 Lakh on Dial4Trade and ExportersIndia, the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said in a statement yesterday.

IndiaMART accounted for the highest number of affected sellers and listings, with 3,092, followed by ExportersIndia with 421, Justdial with 206 and TradeIndia with 166, according to the ministry. Other platforms facing regulatory action include Dial4Trade, Sigma-Aldrich India and Ibuychemikals.

In its statement, the consumer protection body shared that it had issued notices to both Justdial and IndiaMART over the listings. Following the notices, Director General – Investigation investigated the matter and shared their reports with the companies. 

IndiaMART submitted its reply to the investigation report and, subsequently, approached the Delhi High Court challenging the SCN issued by the CCPA. Meanwhile, Justdial has sought adjournments in the matter till now and is yet to respond to the investigation. The next and final hearing in the matter is scheduled to be held on October 23.

 Meanwhile, the CCPA has imposed a penalty of ₹10 Lakh on Dial4Trade for facilitating the sale of ammonium nitrate. ExportersIndia was fined ₹10 Lakh in two separate cases, one involving ammonium nitrate and Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate (PETN), and the other involving picric acid.

The CCPA’s action covers both marketplaces that host third-party sellers and platforms that sell products directly. Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals and Ibuychemikals have told the authority that they sell their own products and do not host third-party sellers. Investigations into TradeIndia, Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals and Ibuychemikals are ongoing.

Dial4Trade challenged the order before the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC), which dismissed its appeal on October 9. The commission held that the listings amounted to misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

ExportersIndia has also appealed against the CCPA’s orders before the NCDRC. The appeals are expected to be listed for hearing in the coming period.

Consumers can report listings of explosives on online platforms through the national consumer helpline at 1915.

Under the Explosives Act, 1884, the sale and purchase of these substances require prescribed licences. The CCPA expects platforms to ensure sellers display valid licences issued by the petroleum and explosives safety organisation (PESO) and verify buyers’ identities and licence status before allowing purchases.

“The action reinforces the Government’s commitment to ensuring that digital marketplaces do not facilitate unauthorised access to regulated or dangerous substances in violation of applicable laws and consumer safety standards,” the ministry said.

item.title: Apple India’s FY26 Profit Jumps 66% YoY To ₹5,311 Cr, Revenue Up 31%
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Apple India reported a 66% year-on-year (YoY) increase in its net profit during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026…
item.content:encoded:
Apple India reported a 66% year-on-year (YoY) increase in its net profit during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26) to ₹5,311 Cr from ₹3,196 Cr it reported in the year-ago period. 

The iPhone-maker’s operating revenue increased 31.4% to ₹1.04 Lakh Cr from ₹79,060 Cr in FY25, buoyed by a significant jump in its sales of iPhone, MacBooks, iPad and other products. 

Apple India’s revenue from the sale of traded goods jumped to ₹99,068 Cr in the period under review, an almost 33% increase from ₹74,680 Cr in FY25. 

Its remaining operating revenue came from its support services, including Apple Care services, which grew 7.6% YoY to 4,292.8 Cr, while revenue from maintenance contracts fetched ₹492.4 Cr. 

Meanwhile, it earned ₹463 Cr from finance income and ₹291 Cr in other income during the fiscal year, taking its total income to ₹1.05 Cr. 

To note, the tech giant had earlier said that its India market operations delivered strong double-digit revenue growth during the June quarter (Q1 FY27), aided by exceptional demand for its more affordable MacBook Neo. 

Apple has continued to deepen its presence in India, expanding beyond its flagship iPhone business into a broader ecosystem spanning Macs, iPads, wearables and services. India has also become central to Apple’s global manufacturing strategy, with the country emerging as one of Apple’s largest production bases outside China. iPhone exports from India crossed ₹2 Lakh Cr in FY26.

It is now expanding its foothold in the country further through its financial services unit Apple Pay, which it launched in India last month in partnership with Axis Bank. The rollout has allowed iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users to make payments in apps, online and at contactless-enabled stores, with Mac support coming soon.

It has already onboarded a host of merchants for Apple Pay, including Apple Store physical locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, Zomato, among others.

Despite the strong growth, the company now expects supply constraints in the coming months due to a shortfall in advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity, along with constraints around memory components. The company expects the constraints to affect availability of iPhones, Macs and iPads globally, which could also have an impact on markets such as India if component shortages persist.

Where Did Apple India Spend In FY26? 

Apple India’s total expenses during the fiscal year under review grew 28% to ₹96,224 Cr from ₹75,190.7 Cr it reported in FY25. Notably, the company paid ₹10,373.7 Cr in license fee during the year, more than double of ₹4,257.8 Cr it spent in FY25.

Purchase Of Traded Goods: Apple India’s inventory expenses stood at ₹78,228.7 Cr during the fiscal year, a 21.6% jump from ₹64,335.8 Cr in FY25, making it the company’s biggest expense. 

Employee Benefit Expenses: Its expenditure under this head surged 13% YoY to ₹3,531.3 from ₹3,126.1 Cr in FY25, including spending on wages, PF contributions, gratuity and staff welfare. Notably, the company paid ₹17,80.4 Cr in salaries and bonuses during the year. 

Marketing & Advertisement: Another major expense head, marketing and advertising cost Apple India ₹1,075.2 Cr during the year, increasing 22.6% YoY from ₹877.1 Cr in the year-ago period.

item.title: IndiQube To Invest ₹35 Cr In Office Space Developer SaiEdge Realty
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Listed coworking space provider IndiQube Spaces’ board has approved an investment of up to ₹35 Cr in SaiEdge Realty to…
item.content:encoded:
Listed coworking space provider IndiQube Spaces’ board has approved an investment of up to ₹35 Cr in SaiEdge Realty to acquire up to a 49% stake.

SaiEdge will develop commercial office spaces that IndiQube intends to lease upon completion, the latter said in an exchange filing 

The investment will be made in cash, in one or more tranches, through subscriptions to equity shares and/or convertible securities.

Incorporated on July 28, SaiEdge has a paid-up share capital of ₹1 Lakh and is yet to commence operations or generate turnover. Its remaining shareholding will be held by other investors.

Separately, IndiQube’s board appointed Ishwar Subramanian as an additional independent director, effective yesterday. His appointment for a five-year term, ending October 18, 2031, is subject to shareholder approval.

The board also reconstituted the company’s audit committee, with Subramanian appointed as chairperson. Independent director Sachi Krishana and executive director and CEO Rishi Das will serve as members.

The appointment follows the resignation of independent director Avalur Gopalaratnam Muralikrishnan, effective yesterday. 

Founded in 2015 by Rishi Das and Meghna Agarwal, Bengaluru-based IndiQube provides managed workspaces to startups, SMEs, and large enterprises. Its offering covers workspace design, interior fit-outs, facilities management, and employee services such as transport. 

The company primarily leases properties and customises them to suit clients’ requirements. It competes with Awfis and Smartworks, among other flexible workspace operators, with its model centred on tailored offices and long-term client relationships. 

IndiQube listed on the bourses in July 2025, following a ₹700 Cr IPO comprising a ₹650 Cr fresh issue and a ₹50 Cr OFS by its cofounders. Its shares debuted at ₹218.70 on the BSE and ₹216 on the NSE, discounts of 7.7% and 8.8%, respectively, to the ₹237 issue price.

On the financial front, IndiQube’s net loss narrowed 35% to ₹23.9 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹36.8 Cr a year earlier. However, loss widened 5% QoQ from ₹22.7 Cr.

Operating revenue grew 37% YoY and 5% QoQ to ₹422.6 Cr. Including other income of ₹26.1 Cr, total income stood at ₹448.7 Cr. The company is yet to report its Q2 FY27 numbers.

item.title: Founder Salaries Tracker FY26: How Much Did India’s Startup Founders Earn?
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Twenty-two founders across 15 new-age tech companies earned a combined ₹66.87 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26, up 2.3% from…
item.content:encoded:
Twenty-two founders across 15 new-age tech companies earned a combined ₹66.87 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26, up 2.3% from ₹65.34 Cr in FY25, according to data compiled by Inc42. Average fixed remuneration per founder increased to ₹3.04 Cr from ₹2.97 Cr.

Of these, 16 founders received increases in fixed pay, four saw reductions, and two reported unchanged remuneration.

Honasa Consumer cofounder Ghazal Alagh recorded the highest percentage increase, with her fixed remuneration rising 60% to ₹2.4 Cr from ₹1.5 Cr. Delhivery cofounder Sahil Barua followed with a 21.4% increase to ₹3.4 Cr from ₹2.8 Cr.

Ola Electric founder Bhavish Aggarwal recorded the steepest percentage decline, with his remuneration falling 34.8% to ₹4.5 Cr from ₹6.9 Cr. Nykaa founder Falguni Nayar’s fixed pay fell 14% to ₹74 Lakh from ₹86 Lakh, while Swiggy cofounder Sriharsha Majety’s remuneration declined 12.5% to ₹1.4 Cr from ₹1.6 Cr.

MobiKwik cofounders Bipin Preet Singh and Upasana Taku topped the list of founders tracked, drawing fixed remuneration of ₹6.3 Cr each in FY26. Lenskart cofounder Peyush Bansal followed at ₹5.7 Cr, down 1.7% from ₹5.8 Cr.

Meesho cofounders Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Kumar each earned ₹4.8 Cr, ahead of Aggarwal at ₹4.5 Cr, Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma at ₹4 Cr, and RateGain founder Bhanu Chopra at ₹3.7 Cr. Sharma’s and Chopra’s fixed remuneration remained unchanged from FY25.

However, fixed pay tells only part of the story. Peyush Bansal received ₹12 Cr in bonuses and performance incentives – more than twice his fixed remuneration – along with perquisites and retirement benefits. Fellow Lenskart cofounder Neha Bansal received ₹6 Cr in bonuses and performance incentives, in addition to her ₹2.7 Cr fixed pay.
Honasa Consumer cofounder Varun Alagh received ₹2.4 Cr in performance incentives, equal to his fixed remuneration.

Share-based compensation also featured prominently. Majety’s ESOP gains stood at ₹549.3 Cr, while Delhivery cofounder Kapil Bharati recorded ₹6.9 Cr in ESOP gains.

Separately, the cost of stock options granted to FirstCry founder Supam Maheshwari stood at ₹31.7 Cr. He also received ₹2.1 Cr in perquisites and ₹84 Lakh in performance incentives.

These components require separate treatment. Stock-option costs and ESOP-related benefits do not necessarily represent cash received by a founder during the year and should be distinguished from fixed salaries and cash incentives.

Inc42 has been tracking founders’ remuneration since FY23, covering the startup ecosystem’s shift from the era of funding boom to the funding winter and now, more recently, towards profitability and IPOs. 

Building on the FY25 edition, the FY26 tracker examines changes in fixed pay, other compensation components, and the financial performance of the companies these founders lead.

item.title: Flipkart Eyes October-End Launch For Food Delivery Service: Report
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Walmart-owned ecommerce major Flipkart is reportedly targeting an October-end public launch for its food delivery service, ‘Eat-in by Minutes’, to…
item.content:encoded:
Walmart-owned ecommerce major Flipkart is reportedly targeting an October-end public launch for its food delivery service, ‘Eat-in by Minutes’, to compete with Eternal-owned Zomato and Swiggy.

The company has expanded its internal pilot in Bengaluru to more than 8,000 employees, according to a TechCrunch report citing people familiar with the development.

National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI) president Sagar Daryani told the publication that Flipkart had informed restaurant partners of plans to launch publicly by October-end and expand to five or six cities by the end of 2026.

Inc42’s queries to Flipkart remained unanswered till the time of publication. The story will be updated on receiving a response.

The expanded trial follows Flipkart’s initial employee pilot in Bengaluru.

Flipkart Taps Ekart, ONDC 

Flipkart’s food delivery service currently appears as a separate tab on its main shopping app, alongside its quick commerce offering Flipkart Minutes and travel bookings. The company has also deployed a dedicated fleet of delivery riders through its logistics arm Ekart, separate from the riders handling quick commerce deliveries.

For restaurant onboarding, Flipkart is tapping the government-backed Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), while also signing up restaurants directly.

The company is positioning its food delivery service around a lower-cost model for restaurant partners. Flipkart has reportedly proposed a base commission of around 10%, as per Daryani. This is much lower than the 20%-25% commission that restaurants typically pay established platforms, he said. 

However, commissions account for only part of restaurants’ costs on food delivery platforms. Advertising, discounts, and promotions add to their overall expenditure, making the total cost of selling through Flipkart an important consideration for prospective partners.

Beyond restaurant pricing, Flipkart’s existing commerce ecosystem gives it a customer base to which it can cross-sell food orders.

Food Delivery Market Sees Fresh Competition

Flipkart’s planned launch comes amid fresh competition for Zomato and Swiggy, with challengers focusing on restaurant commissions and the cost of ordering food online.

Rapido has been expanding Ownly, its food delivery service offering a zero-commission model for restaurants.

Quick food delivery startup Swish has also begun piloting Swish Go, allowing users in select Bengaluru pincodes to order from third-party restaurants and cloud kitchens. The service is advertised as charging no packaging or platform fees.

Similarly, cloud kitchen operator Curefoods announced its MegaBite pilot yesterday, offering dishes priced at ₹49-₹199 from brands across its portfolio. Currently available in Bengaluru’s HSR Layout, the app claims to charge no delivery or platform fees.

These moves reflect growing pressure on incumbent platforms to offer more affordable options to customers while addressing restaurant partners’ concerns over platform commissions and promotional expenses.

For Flipkart, food delivery adds another business alongside its expanding quick commerce operations through Minutes.

The expansion also comes amid uncertainty over its IPO timeline. Former senior executives, including Mukesh Bansal, Sanjay Baweja, and Ankit Nagori, have urged Walmart to buy back their vested ESOPs. 

On the financial front, the Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% YoY jump in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in FY26, while its consolidated net loss narrowed marginally by 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr from ₹8,646 Cr in FY25.

item.title: Centre Mulls Hardware Security Layer For Starlink, Other Satcom Operators
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: The Centre is reportedly considering developing a hardware device to strengthen security oversight of satellite internet services offered by Starlink…
item.content:encoded:
The Centre is reportedly considering developing a hardware device to strengthen security oversight of satellite internet services offered by Starlink and other overseas operators.

The proposed device would act as a control layer between users and satellite networks, with all satellite traffic routed through it, ET reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. The hardware could be installed at subscriber premises or satellite ground stations.

The government is considering involving public sector R&D units with communications technology expertise, while keeping participation by select private players open.

An official cited in the report said the security layer would address risks associated with foreign satellite operators that may be treated as untrusted transport carriers. The proposal remains under discussion, with its technical specifications and implementation timeline yet to be finalised.

Satellite broadband could help connect remote communities and businesses where terrestrial networks are difficult or expensive to deploy.

Starlink, Jio, OneWeb Await Clearances

The development comes after Elon Musk accused Indian business interests of blocking Starlink’s entry to protect their telecom operations. He also targeted Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani, questioning whether he was the “real boss of India”.

Reliance rejected the allegations, saying it welcomed competition, including from Starlink. It added that Jio’s satellite services were also awaiting government clearances.

The Ministry of Communications also denied allegations of preferential treatment, maintaining that Starlink, Reliance Jio Satellite Communications, and Bharti Enterprises-backed Eutelsat OneWeb are at broadly the same regulatory stage.

All three operators have received Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite (GMPCS) licences. However, they must complete security assessments and meet the relevant conditions before spectrum can be assigned and commercial services launched.

Obtaining a licence and IN-SPACe authorisation does not mean an operator has completed its security assessment or secured spectrum.

Security Concerns Drive Scrutiny

The proposed hardware layer reflects concerns about foreign operators controlling critical communications infrastructure, particularly during conflicts or other national security emergencies.

Starlink’s role in Ukraine has brought such risks into focus, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accusing the company of slowing connection speeds and impeding operations during the conflict with Russia. Other countries like Iran and South Africa also raised concerns about Starlink’s operations or authorisations in the past.

Speaking to Inc42 last week, Innefu Labs cofounder and CEO Tarun Wig said foreign-controlled satellite networks could create risks around data sovereignty, service continuity, and external control over critical communications infrastructure. However, he said that the circumstances in Ukraine did not automatically mean India would face the same risks.

Quantive Advisory founder Sohom Banerjee highlighted operational checks covering who can activate terminals, change routing or coverage, access sensitive network information, and suspend services.

item.content:encoded:
Brokerages Get A Ticket To Wall Street 

The Nifty 50 has dropped 12.4% YTD in 2026, the first yearly decline in over a decade, and FPIs had pulled a cumulative ₹3.1 Lakh Cr (around $33 Bn) over this time from Indian equities. With the stock market sliding and SIPs returning negative returns, retail investors also want to hedge bets against rallying US tech stocks. A clutch of discount brokerages like Zerodha, Groww, Angel One and Upstox are now enabling this exposure. So, what’s on offer?

Green Card For Indian Folios: Zerodha is now offering eligible users an option to invest in up to 2,000 US-listed companies and around 1,000 ETFs through its Kite platform. Users can opt for fractional investing, same-day delivery or SIPs. Funds can simply be transferred to dollar-denominated wallets through net banking, with UPI and card payments yet to be introduced. 

Desi Discount Brokers Go Global: Peers like Groww and Upstoxx had already launched similar offerings recently, with Angel One also joining the club on Monday. All four received approval from the International Financial Services Centres Authority in June to offer investors international and US stock options from GIFT City. Prior to this, IND Money and HDFC Securities were popular platforms for international investing. 

US Stocks Take The Cake: Direct exposure to international markets will allow Indian investors to not only hedge domestic concentration and diversify geographical risk, but also gain access to global technology megatrends like AI, cloud computing, and semiconductors, which are yet to enter Indian equity markets meaningfully. 

Brokers Eye Revenue Mix: The market slowdown in India, combined with SEBI’s derivatives reforms, is squeezing discount brokers’ core trading income, forcing them to diversify into lending and allied financial services. New demat account additions were down 22% YoY to 3.2 Cr in FY26, and discount brokers need to cross-sell more exciting products to existing users, making US stocks an enticing choice. 

So, as Indian investors look beyond domestic markets, here’s what Zerodha and its peers have to offer now…

From The Editor’s Desk

Tonbo Imaging’s IPO Concludes With A Bang 

  • The defence tech startup’s ₹852.1 Cr IPO was subscribed almost 140X on the final day of bidding, receiving bids for 115.87 Cr shares against the 85.3 Lakh shares on offer. 
  • QIBs led the demand with a 293.56X subscription of their quota, followed by NIIs at 170.94X, while retail investors bid for 31.07X their allotted shares. 
  • Tonbo’s IPO comprises only an OFS of up to 1.22 Cr shares, with a price band of ₹665–₹700 per share valuing the company at around ₹4,010 Cr at the upper end. 

Even Healthcare Bags $50 Mn

  • Even Healthcare raised $50 Mn in a Series B round led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from Alpha Wave, to expand its hospital network across Bengaluru.
  • Founded in 2020, the startup operates a managed-care model combining preventive healthcare, diagnostics, hospitalisation and post-discharge recovery. It has raised a total of $120 Mn in funding to date. 
  • The startup plans to open one hospital by end-2026 and three more by end-FY27 before expanding to more cities, while shifting focus towards hospital-led healthcare.

Curefoods Enters Budget Food Delivery

  • Curefoods is piloting MegaBite in Bengaluru’s HSR Layout, offering dishes priced at ₹49–₹199 from its brands, including Rolls On Wheels, Olio Pizza, and Eatfit, with no delivery charges or platform fees.
  • Founded in 2020 by Cult.fit founder Ankit Nagori, Curefoods has built a cloud kitchen portfolio through acquisitions. It paused its IPO process after receiving the SEBI nod due to valuation concerns. 
  • This is the startup’s first attempt at running its own delivery platform, placing it in direct competition with other budget food providers like Swiggy’s Toing, Rapido’s Ownly and Rebel Foods’ EatSure. 

Hunar.AI’s Agentic Hiring Bet

  • Bengaluru-based Hunar.AI raised ₹40 Cr ($4.2 Mn) in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures, with participation from existing and new investors. The funds will strengthen its AI infrastructure, products and go-to-market strategy.
  • Founded in 2022 by Krishna Khandelwal and Shantanu Bhattacharyya, Hunar.AI is building conversational AI agents to automate frontline hiring, onboarding, training and employee retention across multiple industries.
  • Hunar.AI claims its agents handled over 1.5 Cr conversations through September 2026, with volumes doubling QoQ. Its customers include Swiggy, Zepto, Croma, Starbucks and Bajaj Finserv.

Meta Faces Meity Algorithm Review

  • The IT ministry has asked Meta to review Facebook and Instagram’s recommendation algorithms to prevent misleading or out-of-context content from being disproportionately amplified and to promote diverse, credible information.
  • Meta has faced repeated scrutiny this year over its content moderation policies and the availability of CSAM on its platforms, resulting in stricter reporting guidelines. 
  • The October 10 advisory calls for stronger content-review mechanisms, contextual information on visuals depicting public events, and faster escalation of posts that could trigger public confusion or disorder.

Inc42 Markets

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

How Factrika Is Solving Blue-Collar Hiring Gaps For Factory

Manufacturers can lose valuable production time when workers fail to turn up, or demand spikes leave them short-staffed. To address this, Factrika is building an on-demand workforce platform that helps factories source, deploy and manage blue-collar workers based on skills, location and shift requirements.

Staffing On Demand: Founded in 2024 by Kshitij Puri and Gaurav Asthana, the New Delhi-based startup offers same-day staffing, absentee replacement, seasonal workforce deployment, project-based hiring and full-time recruitment. Its platform coordinates worker deployment, tracks attendance and arranges replacements when workers fail to show up.

Building A Factory Workforce: Factrika claims to have access to more than 10,000 workers through a network spanning over 4,000 ITIs and 1,000 polytechnic institutes. It says it has completed over 65,000 shifts with a 90% job-fill rate, operating across Bhiwadi, Bawal, Kharkhoda, Gurugram and Bahadurgarh. Its customers include Lenskart, Asahi India Glass and Jubilant FoodWorks.

Scaling Operations: Factrika recently raised ₹8.9 Cr to expand its team, strengthen its technology and enter more manufacturing clusters. As factories contend with fluctuating labour requirements and tight delivery schedules, the startup is betting that on-demand staffing will make shop-floor workforce management less chaotic. 

As manufacturers look for faster, more reliable ways to fill shop-floor roles, can Factrika become the go-to workforce platform for India’s factories?

item.title: What’s Cooking In Smart Kitchens?
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Food has a way of taking us back in time. A familiar aroma or a single bite can bring back…
item.content:encoded:
Food has a way of taking us back in time. A familiar aroma or a single bite can bring back memories. For some, it may be their Nani’s dal fry; for others, their mother’s achaar — a taste passed down through generations. Yet, no matter how many times we try to recreate these dishes, they rarely taste quite like the originals.  

Unfortunately, with busy schedules, long commutes and the demands of everyday life, finding time to cook a meal is not always easy. The pandemic, however, offered an opportunity, and people did return to their kitchens, dusted off family recipes and learnt to cook meals they would otherwise have ordered online. 

But as offices reopened, so did the daily grind. For professionals, it became a herculean task to fit cooking into their busy routines. This is where AI-powered cooking assistants have found an opening, according to Mahek Mody, the founder of upliance.ai, a provider of smart cooking appliances.   

“People want to eat home-cooked food, but there are two things we need to do to get people to cook at home. First, make it convenient. Second, make it interesting,” Mody said, adding that by combining automated cooking functions with guided recipes and software that can be updated or improved over time, advanced cooking appliances are making home cooking less time-consuming and more accessible.

In India, a growing set of players, including established brands such as Wonderchef and Philips, is betting on this proposition. Their products range from guided cooking machines to more automated devices that handle multiple steps of a recipe.

But the opportunity is still in its nascency. While these appliances promise to bridge the gap between wanting home-cooked food and having the time to prepare it, their relatively high prices raise questions about the size of the addressable market, who will pay for them, and whether they can move beyond early adopters to become a fixture in Indian kitchens. Let’s find out…

India’s Smart Kitchen Shift

From the perfect tadka to that secret family ingredient, every Indian kitchen has its own way of doing things. For automated cooking to catch on, these appliances must get the Indian palate right. This is where AI, data and machine learning can help. 

At upliance, the company uses generative AI to translate recipes into instructions that its appliance can execute. For instance, its YouTube recipe feature breaks down a cooking video into steps and maps them to the device’s capabilities, from chopping ingredients to adjusting cooking sequences. AI also helps identify cooking styles and adapt recipes to Indian preferences.

Customers can also access recipes through the company’s app and leave a voicemail if something goes wrong while cooking. The team responds to their queries and uses ratings and feedback to improve recipes over time.

“A general-purpose AI chatbot can explain how to cook something, but it cannot necessarily send instructions to a physical device that performs the cooking. Connecting AI-generated instructions to the appliance is the distinction we are trying to create,” Mody said.

Machine learning helps the appliance respond to variations during cooking. He said data from several lakh tadka preparations has helped the company refine its algorithms. 

However, not everyone in the category believes such capabilities should automatically be labelled AI. The founder of Wonderchef, Ravi Saxena, argued that many features marketed as AI-powered are based on connectivity, memory or basic analytics.

“Wonderchef’s appliances, too, can download recipes from the internet. There is a limited role for AI in improving our products, and we do not want to exaggerate that role,” Saxena said. 

The company also analyses usage patterns to improve cooking instructions. If users consistently boil a dish for 18 minutes instead of the recommended 15, the company can spot the trend and adjust the recipe accordingly. The appliances can also track how users vary ingredient quantities while cooking. According to him, these improvements do not necessarily require AI. 

AI In The Kitchen: What’s Driving Adoption? 

According to MarkNtel Advisors Research, India’s smart kitchen appliances market is estimated at $800 Mn-$1.48 Bn in 2026. Cooking appliances account for approximately 48% of the market. AI-powered cooking assistants and automated kitchen appliances, including products from upliance and Wonderchef, also fall within this broader segment. 

Besides, new-age brands such as Nosh, Posha, On2Cook and Geek Robocook are also betting on the emerging segment. Meanwhile, legacy players like Philips are entering the space, with the company launching its automated, all-in-one smart cooking device, Philips OneChef, in India earlier this year. 

But Wonderchef’s Saxena believes the category is still some way from a tipping point. He compared it with air fryers — a category that took seven years to gain widespread adoption. Automated cooking appliances will similarly need consumer education, while excessive complexity and higher prices in the name of AI could deter buyers.

Repeat usage offers one sign of whether these products are becoming part of everyday kitchens. Saxena says Wonderchef’s Roti Magic is used daily by its buyers, Chai Magic around three times a day, and Chef Magic roughly three times a week. 

Similarly, upliance reported that more than 7,000 Indian households have cooked 6.68 Lakh meals on its platform since December 2022. 

The Conundrum

As of now, the segment is plagued with white-labelled products, which has its own demerits. Factors such as inconsistent cooking results, the need for manual intervention and cleaning hassles raise questions about the hands-free convenience these appliances promise. 

According to Saxena, at ₹30,000 or more, buyers expect consistent results and convenience, not another appliance gathering dust in the kitchen. 

Ravi of upliance said that many products in the industry may look similar but fail to deliver on their promises and compromise on pillars like post-sale services while pushing up customer acquisition costs, giving a bad name to peers offering real innovation and satisfactory aftersales. 

“The base of this problem is white labelling,” he said. Mody also argued that having an IP can open the room for improving it over time, unlike selling a fixed third-party product.

While the technology and price point may appeal to a specific segment of Indian consumers, reaching a wider market remains a challenge. At the same time, high upfront costs could limit adoption, making affordability and the ability to deliver consistent value crucial to scaling the category.

Archana Jahagirdar of Rukam Capital proposes a solution — designing regionally suitable cooking assistants that provide functional value and are available at affordable prices. “But the success of AI-powered cooking assistants will ultimately depend on how well brands balance convenience, affordability and reliability,” she said. 

All in all, while technology can make home cooking easier, winning over Indian households will require more than smart features. Products must cater to regional tastes, deliver consistent results and offer value for money to move beyond early adopters and become everyday kitchen essentials. 

THE STARTUP SPOTLIGHT | HOW EATNACK IS PUTTING A HEALTHY SPIN ON SNACKING

  • EatNack sells health-focused snacks and convenient meal options, positioning itself around the idea of combining taste, nutrition and convenience. It uses processes such as freeze-drying and steam-roasting to retain taste and nutrients while avoiding artificial additives.
  • Its portfolio spans snacks such as masala almonds, lime-and-mint peanuts and seasoned cashews, alongside ready-to-eat meal options. It has 11–20 SKUs across its product range that clock an average MRR of ₹3.5 Lakh.
  • Marketplaces contribute to 70% of sales, offline channels account for 25%, and its own website generates the remaining 5%. The brand is now targeting institutional and hospitality customers, alongside opportunities in export markets like Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the UAE and Mauritius. 

The Deep Dive

ECOMMERCE BUZZ

The Operator Question

When a consumer is willing to spend ₹50,000 on an AI-powered cooking assistant, what factors determine their choice between legacy appliance players and newer AI-first brands, and how can brands differentiate themselves beyond price? 

In conversation with Inc42, Nosh founder Yatin Varachhiya said that at ₹50,000, consumers will choose a product that gives them clear, distinct value. 

Such a product should be able to solve an everyday need by cooking complete meals independently, allowing people to enjoy cuisines from around the world using ingredients they know and trust. 

Beyond price, many differentiate through true autonomy, everyday convenience, and an experience that consumers cannot get from a traditional kitchen appliance.

item.content:encoded:
Ahead of opening its public issue on Wednesday (October 19), telecom major Jio Platforms has raised ₹8,109.8 Cr from anchor investors. 

The company allotted 7.25 Cr equity shares to anchor investors at a price of ₹1,119 per share, the upper end of its price band. 

Around 2.48 Cr shares, more than a third of the overall, were picked up by 25 domestic mutual funds via a total of 95 schemes. Domestic mutual funds that anchored Jio’s IPO were  SBI Mutual Funds, HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, among others. 

Besides, 97 Lakh equity shares (13.4% of the anchor round) were picked up by insurance companies and pension funds including Life Insurance Corporation of India, HDFC Life Insurance, SBI Life Insurance, and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance. 

Global investors such as Fidelity, Allianz, BlackRock, Government of Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Goldman Sachs also picked up stakes in Jio ahead of its IPO. 

Earlier in the day, it was reported that the anchor book has attracted demand of more than 30X its size. As per reports, Jio commands a grey market premium of ₹260, indicating a potential premium listing. The company is expected to get listed on the bourses on October 28.

The IPO, which comprises a fresh issue of up to 27 Cr equity shares, will open for public subscription on October 21 and close on October 23. 

Jio is seeking to raise ₹30,213 Cr at the upper end of the price band, making it India’s largest public offering till date. This pricing would imply a valuation of ₹10.3 Lakh Cr for the telecom major.

The company expects to use the fresh capital generated from the IPO to reduce its subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd’s (RJIL), net debt and interest burden, and improve its leverage.

The proposed repayment covers three external commercial borrowing (ECB) facilities worth a combined ₹29,971 Cr, secured from a consortium of Indian and international lenders, including SBI, Bank of America and First Abu Dhabi Bank. 

The loans were originally raised to fund 5G infrastructure deployment and spectrum acquisition, with repayments scheduled between March and June 2028. Their interest rates range from 1.40% to 5.13% per annum.

The remaining proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes may be used for strategic initiatives, growth opportunities, capital expenditure, working capital, marketing and other business requirements.

Jio Platforms reported a 9.2% YoY increase in consolidated net profit to ₹7,764 Cr in Q1 FY27, from ₹7,110 Cr a year earlier. Operating revenue rose 11.8% YoY and 2.4% QoQ to ₹39,173 Cr, while gross revenue grew 12% YoY to ₹45,961 Cr.

item.title: FSSAI Crackdown Continues With Fresh Show-Cause Notices Issued To Zepto, Others
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued show-cause notices to quick commerce unicorn Zepto as well…
item.content:encoded:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued show-cause notices to quick commerce unicorn Zepto as well as several food and nutraceutical brands amid a broader crackdown on food safety violations. 

The notice against Zepto followed a consumer complaint on social media alleging delivery of expired packets of besan (gram flour). The regulator directed the platform to submit order logs, seller details, warehouse tracking, root-cause analysis, and proof of stock withdrawal and customer refunds. 

Besides Zepto, nutraceutical brands BMS Lifescience and HealthyHey Foods, as well as bakery brand Bakelite Food Processing, received show-cause notices over misleading labelling and advertising. 

  • Bakelite: The parent company behind Pune-based Malpani Foods was targeted over describing its product, ‘Malpani’s Bakelite Puneri Cream Roll’, as ‘creamy’. However, the product includes no cream or  any other dairy-based ingredients but hydrogenated vegetable fat, margarine, and sugar. 
  • BMS Lifescience: The brand was marketing ‘HAOG’s Cranberry Urinary Tract Health Capsules’ under an expired FSSAI registration certificate, and also made health-related claims around disease risk reduction pertaining to the kidney and urinary tract without approval from the regulator. It was also pulled up for misleading usage of the official FSSAI logo, non-compliant use of the claim “as directed by healthcare practitioner”, and making potentially misleading claims online. 
  • HealthyHey Foods: The regulator called out the brand for discrepancies in labelled ingredients across its website and Flipkart regarding its “HealthyHey Nutrition Natural Cranberry Extract 25% Capsules”. It further alleged the brand was making unapproved claims like “100% Natural”; and marketing the product with the FSSAI logo and “FSSAI certified” in a misleading way. 

The regulator has directed all the companies to submit comprehensive written explanations and corrective action reports within stipulated deadlines or face license suspensions and statutory penalties. 

Just days earlier, the regulator pulled up BigBasket and Flipkart over misleading promotions carried by products sold on the respective platforms. 

Besides, the FSSAI has also sanctioned adjudication proceedings against beverage brand Storia. It had earlier flagged the brand’s pomegranate juice for containing only 4% pomegranate juice concentrate and 12% apple juice concentrate, in spite of misleading front-of-pack branding and visual imagery. 

The authority had also cited non-compliant declarations, including prominent “No Added Sugar” claims alongside obscured disclosures, and the unapproved claim “Equivalent to 100% Fruit Juice (Reconstituted)”.

Notably, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) had also fined the brand ₹1 Lakh for misleading consumers. The consumer protection body pulled up Storia for using the branding “100%” in their product labelling, due to reconstituted ingredients and lack of evidence. 

The latest series of notices fits into a larger pattern of the FSSAI identifying illegal food labelling and marketing practices on products sold online. Till now, it has also penalised multiple platforms — Amazon, Bigbasket, Flipkart, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto — for allegedly engaging in misbranding, misleading claims, and sale and display of prohibited or poisonous food articles. 

For Zepto, the fresh regulatory scrutiny adds on to legal issues the quick commerce major has been facing ahead of its proposed public plans. 

Zepto disclosed multiple ongoing regulatory and labour-related proceedings in its updated DRHP, which was filed with the markets regulator SEBI earlier in June.

These include consumer protection cases over alleged dark patterns, food safety violations as well as an Enforcement Directorate inquiry into its ownership structure under FEMA. The company’s subsidiary has also faced allegations of overcharging beyond MRP and misleading advertisements. Other pending matters involve alleged wage underpayment, trade licence violations and food safety issues across several states. 

Besides the regulatory challenges, Zepto had faced unalignment with institutional investors over its IPO valuations which led the company to pause its IPO until May 2027. The quick commerce major is currently chasing a pre-IPO placement of about ₹1,000 Cr.

item.title: Justdial’s Q2 Net Profit Slides 10% YoY To ₹108 Cr Despite 13% Revenue Growth
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Online classifieds platform Justdial’s net profit for the September 2026 quarter (Q2 FY27) dipped 9.7% YoY to ₹107.8 Cr from…
item.content:encoded:
Online classifieds platform Justdial’s net profit for the September 2026 quarter (Q2 FY27) dipped 9.7% YoY to ₹107.8 Cr from ₹119.4 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, the company’s net profit plunged 35.1% from ₹166.2 Cr in the June quarter.

The company’s operating revenue, on the other hand, rose 13.1% YoY and 4.7% QoQ to ₹342.8 Cr.

The decline in net profit came amid a fall in other income, which dropped 25.6% YoY and 58.5% QoQ to ₹54.6 Cr. The company attributed the sequential decline to movements in bond yields. Yields rose around 57 basis points (bps) during the September quarter, compared with a decline of around 44 bps in Q1 FY27, when the company recorded higher mark-to-market (MTM) gains.

The company’s expenses for the quarter rose 15% YoY to ₹262.8 Cr. Tax expenses for the quarter stood at ₹26.8 Cr.

Justdial’s operating EBITDA rose 4.1% to ₹90.7 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹87.1 Cr in the year-ago quarter. However, its operating EBITDA margin contracted 228 bps YoY to 26.4% from 28.7% a year earlier.

The company said investments in AI-led capabilities, automation and B2B expansion accounted for approximately one-third of incremental expenditure during the quarter. These investments are aimed at improving the platform’s capabilities and helping merchants acquire customers and manage their businesses.

Justdial Paid Campaigns, Listings Grows

On the operational front, Justdial recorded 19.84 Cr unique visitors during Q2 FY27, up 0.4% YoY and 2.8% QoQ.

Mobile platforms accounted for 85.1% of the traffic, or 16.89 Cr unique visitors. Desktop and PC platforms contributed 2.45 Cr visitors, accounting for 12.4% of the total, while the voice platform accounted for the remaining 50 Lakh visitors.

While mobile traffic declined 2.1% YoY, desktop and PC traffic grew 24.7%. Voice traffic, meanwhile, fell 9.2% over the same period.

The company’s total active business listings increased 12.2% YoY to 5.74 Cr at the end of September. Justdial added a net 13.1 Lakh listings during the quarter, down 13.8% from 15.2 Lakh additions in the year-ago period.

Paid campaigns on the platform grew 5.2% YoY and 2.7% QoQ to 6.57 Lakh. Total app downloads reached 4.49 Cr, up 7.8% YoY, although average daily downloads declined 21.9% to 6,363.

Alongside its core local business discovery and lead-generation operations, Justdial is expanding its merchant offerings through AI-powered tools and business management products.

The company is developing capabilities to help merchants manage their digital presence, customer interactions and lead pipelines. Its product suite includes JD Business, a dashboard for managing campaigns, enquiries and performance, and JD Omni, which offers business tools, analytics and an online store, alongside a website builder.

Justdial CEO Dinkar Ayilavarapu said the company is now focused on strengthening its core business, helping merchants manage their digital presence and customer conversations, and building products that increase the value of merchant relationships.

The company is also exploring opportunities to expand beyond discovery and lead generation into a broader marketplace of business services and AI-powered tools for merchant operations.

“Looking further ahead, Justdial sees opportunities to extend its platform beyond discovery and lead generation by addressing a broader range of merchant needs. Potential areas include connecting businesses with relevant services through a marketplace, developing AI-powered tools to support business operations, and applying its merchant intelligence and context to enable new digital services,” the company said.

Shares of Justdial ended today’s trading session 2.82% higher at ₹732.55.

item.title: Curefoods Pilots Budget Food Delivery App MegaBite

item.content:encoded:
In a bid to expand into the budget food delivery segment, cloud kitchen operator Curefoods has begun piloting a new service, MegaBite, in Bengaluru.  

Available on the Play Store and App Store, MegaBite appears to serve dishes — in the range of ₹49-₹199 — from restaurants across its brand portfolio. Dishes from Rolls On Wheels, Olio Pizza, Krispy Kreme, Eatfit, Arambam, among others, are live on the platform. 

The app is currently operational only in Bengaluru’s HSR Layout and claims to charge “no delivery charges” and “no platform fee”. The company’s founder and CEO Ankit Nagori announced the launch on social media today.

MegaBite is being marketed as “built for value-conscious, digitally-savvy consumers” and claims to make food delivery “faster, more affordable, and convenient”.

However, much hasn’t been shared by the IPO-bound company. The company declined to respond to Inc42 on our queries regarding the launch. 

Curefoods follows suit as food delivery competitors are focused on reducing fees and commissions. Rapido’s Ownly, Swiggy’s Toing and Swish Go are some such names that are increasingly doubling down on this proposition. 

To note, this would be the first attempt Curefoods is operating its own delivery platform. It’s unclear as of now if Curefoods itself will handle delivery and fulfilment or if it will join hands with third-party logistics partners. 

Interestingly, rival cloud kitchen operator Rebel Foods has long operated its own delivery app EatSure, which competes with Swiggy and Zomato with offerings from restaurant brands it owns. The startup had also launched a 15-minute food delivery app QuickiES, which it shut down earlier this year, after almost one year of operations. 

Founded in 2020 by ex-Flipkart executive Nagori, Curefoods started off as ‘Eat.fit’, a food brand under the umbrella of fitness startup Cult.fit, but later broke off into a separate business. It has since grown to become a complete house of brands following an elaborate acquisition strategy for expansion. 

The startup has raised $150 Mn to date from the likes of Accel, Iron Pillar and 3State Ventures. Notably, it secured the green light from market regulator SEBI for a public listing around a year ago. The proposed IPO would comprise a fresh issue of ₹800 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 4.85 Cr equity shares. 

However, Curefoods later put its plans on hold after mutual funds reportedly raised concerns around its desired valuation of ₹4,000 Cr, given market volatility.

item.title: Hunar Raises ₹40 Cr To Scale Agentic AI For Frontline Hiring
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Hiring thousands of frontline workers (employees who directly provide goods and services to communities) across multiple cities is a coordination-heavy…
item.content:encoded:
Hiring thousands of frontline workers (employees who directly provide goods and services to communities) across multiple cities is a coordination-heavy cumbersome task for HR managers. Recruiters have to call prospective employees, follow up on applications, schedule interviews and keep workers informed through onboarding and training. 

When hiring volumes spike during festive seasons or business expansion, these tasks can quickly become more difficult to solve manually. Bengaluru-based conversational AI startup Hunar.AI is building AI agents to automate these HR workflows. 

The startup today announced the raise of ₹40 Cr ($4.2 Mn) in its Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. Other investors like Hyderabad Angels Fund, Together Fund, Seedstars, AVNM Ventures, PhysicsWallah cofounders Prateek Maheshwari and Alakh Pandey, and MediaMint cofounder Aditya Vuchi also participated in the round. 

Founded in 2022 by Krishna Khandelwal and Shantanu Bhattacharyya, Hunar.AI automates frontline workforce management via its conversational AI agents. These agents help ease various frontline workforce management issues — including hiring, onboarding, training and retention. 

It is targeting businesses that need to recruit and manage large numbers of workers, often across several locations and regional languages.

The startup offers voice AI capabilities in more than 20 languages, including Tamil, Telugu and Kannada. This allows enterprises to communicate with workers in their preferred languages while automating workflows that would otherwise require repeated calls and manual follow-ups.

The startup intends to use the fresh capital to strengthen its AI infrastructure, develop its products and bolster its go-to-market strategy.

“Frontline workforce management is one of the largest yet most underserved opportunities in enterprise AI. Solving it requires more than applying general-purpose models to existing processes. It demands a deep understanding of industry workflows, multilingual capabilities and technology that can reliably execute tasks at scale,” said cofounder and CEO Krishna Khandelwal.

The startup claims its AI agents handled more than 1.5 Cr conversations till September 2026, with volumes doubling quarter-on-quarter. Its customers include Swiggy, Zepto, Aditya Birla Capital, Bajaj Finserv, Croma, Dr Lal PathLabs, 1mg and Starbucks.

AI Targets India’s Growing Frontline Workforce

The startup is targeting a workforce segment that spans quick commerce, ecommerce, logistics, mobility, retail and financial services. These businesses often need to recruit workers quickly across multiple cities, while keeping communication and onboarding processes running at scale.

The market size is also expanding. According to NITI Aayog projections, India’s gig workforce is expected to grow from approximately 1 Cr workers in FY25 to 2.35 Cr by 2029-30.

While more workforce helps in finding the right candidates, keeping applicants engaged, coordinating onboarding and ensuring workers receive the necessary information requires manual effort. This is more relevant when recruitment is spread across regions with different languages.

The startup’s approach is to automate these interactions through conversational agents designed around specific enterprise workflows, rather than offer a general-purpose chatbot. Its ability to handle regional languages and integrate into existing workforce processes will be central to how effectively it can serve large employers.

The latest funding will help the startup build out that technology and expand its reach among enterprises.
